# The 13.2 notes' wide frames overflow the Portal column at laptop widths

## Context

#19517 embedded the 13.2 release notes' frames at `width="760"` (D4 at 360). The premise was that the attribute width keeps each image inside the Portal's column, and it rested on one measurement: a 785 px column at a 1440 px viewport. Grace's #19520 then found the blog column at 685 px and switched the posts' wide frames to `width="100%"`.

I measured the release view's column across viewports. Setup: local Portal (`neo-dev-server`), `#/news/releases/13.1.0`, the `.neo-markdown-component` content box.

| viewport | 1024 | 1280 | 1366 | 1440 | 1536 | 1920 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| column (px) | 619 | 875 | **711** | 785 | 881 | 1104 |

The column is not monotonic. At 1280 the side navigation collapses, so the column widens; at 1366 the navigation returns.

## The Problem

`.neo-markdown-image-wrapper` keeps an image at its attribute width (`max-width: initial`, `overflow-x: auto`, the `#8479` design). A 760 px frame therefore scrolls inside its box wherever the column is narrower: 49 px hidden at 1366 and 141 px at 1024. A fixed pixel width cannot fit a responsive column; `width="100%"` fills it at every width.

## The Fix

`.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v13.2.0.md`: the seven wide frames (D1, D2, D3, the native return, the grid cell edit, FM-1, FM-2) take `width="100%"`. D4 keeps `width="360"`, a narrow frame that fits every measured column. Captions and alt texts are unchanged. GitHub renders `width="100%"` at its own column width.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: every wide frame carries `width="100%"`, D4 keeps 360, and captions are unchanged. The release-note link scan passes, and `marked` emits the eight `<img>`, each followed by its caption.
- [ ] AC-2: the 13.2 notes rendered in the local Portal at 1024, 1366, 1440 and 1920 px: no image box scrolls (`scrollWidth == clientWidth`) and every image loads.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] The GitHub render of the notes shows the eight frames.

## Out of Scope

- The blog posts (#19519 / #19520).
- The Portal's image box itself (`#8479`).
